newsitem.title: USA: BPA raises firm peak power 50 cents/MWh for Friday.
newsitem.headline: BPA raises firm peak power 50 cents/MWh for Friday.

text.p: The Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) raised prices for firm on-peak power on Friday by 50 cents per megawatt hour (MWh) and refrained from offering any non-firm peak power, the agency said Thursday.
BPA offered up to 300 megawatts of firm power during peak demand hours at $13.50 per MWh for Northwest deliveries and $14.50 for California-Oregon border (COB) sales.
Friday firm off-peak prices were unchanged at $9.00 per MWh for all deliveries.

Non-firm power prices for off-peak (0100-0500 and 2400 PST) were unchanged at $9.00 for all deliveries, while prices for shoulder hours (0600-0700, 1100-1700 and 2100-2200) were separated at $10.00 for Northwest and $11.00 for COB.
BPA also offered displacement power during off-peak hours on Friday at $7.00 per MWh.
BPA's Saturday off-peak prices were largely in line with Friday, while peak firm power was offered at $12.50 (Northwest) and $13.50 (COB).
Non-firm peak power for Saturday was offered at $16.00 for Northwest deliveries and $17.00 for COB.
